title: Incentive Misalignment + Evaluation Gaming: How Governance Failures Enable Benchmark Overfitting

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if safety benchmark overfitting is empirically confirmed, it demonstrates that a core governance mechanism is actively misleading. This would motivate held-out evaluation practices.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: requires access to evaluation history data for models across multiple benchmark versions. Finding models with multiple evaluation points on both known and novel benchmarks may be data-limited.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: collecting evaluation histories, distinguishing known vs. novel benchmarks, and computing improvement rates requires significant data gathering and methodological care.

novelty.reasoning: This topic has received substantial recent attention. 'Can We Trust AI Benchmarks? An Interdisciplinary Review of Current Issues in AI Evaluation' (arXiv:2502.06559, 2025) comprehensively covers benchmark overfitting, data contamination, and incentive misalignment. 'Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?' (arXiv:2407.21792, 2024) directly addresses whether safety benchmarks are gamed. 'Bench-2-CoP' (arXiv:2508.05464, 2025) analyzes benchmarks for EU AI Act compliance gaps. The finding that analysis of 194,000+ benchmark questions reveals stark misalignment between evaluation practices and risk frameworks is published. 'AI Testing Should Account for Sophisticated Strategic Behaviour' (arXiv:2508.14927, 2025) covers evaluation gaming. The proposed contribution is largely covered by this existing literature.
